title: 和, 也, 都: and, also, all
summary: Lets you join two nouns with 和 and say also and all with 也 and 都, which come before the verb.
structure: Subject (two or more) + 都 + Verb (+ Object)
explanation:
和 means "and", but only between nouns, that is, people and things: 我和你 (you and me), 茶和水 (tea and water). Don't use 和 to join two whole sentences. To say "I'm a student and he's a teacher", just put a comma between the two sentences: 我是学生，他是老师。

也 means "also, too", and 都 means "all, both". Both words go right after the subject and before the verb, never at the start of the sentence and never after the verb: 我也是学生 (I'm a student too), 我们都是学生 (we are all students).

都 sums up a group that has already been mentioned before it, so the subject needs to be more than one person or thing: 我们, 他们, 爸爸和妈妈. A common combination is 和 + 都: 我和他都喜欢猫 (he and I both like cats).

You can use both words together. The order is always 也都: 他们也都是老师 (they are all teachers too). To say "not", put 不 after them: 我也不喝 (I don't drink it either), 我们都不去 (none of us are going).

examples.en: My mom and I drink tea.
I'm a student, and he's a student too.

examples.zh: 我爸爸和我妈妈都是老师。
examples.en: My dad and my mom are both teachers.

examples.zh: 我哥哥和弟弟也都在中国。
examples.en: My older brother and my younger brother are both in China too.

mistakes.why: 也 never starts the sentence. It goes after the subject and before the verb.
都 goes before the verb, and 是 is the verb here. So 都 comes before 是.
和 only joins nouns like 我和他. It can't join two sentences. Use a comma instead.

exercises.en: He likes drinking tea, and I like drinking tea too.
why: 也 means "too" and goes after the subject 我, before the verb 喜欢.
和 only joins two nouns, like 我和他. It can't stand before a verb.
都 means "all/both" and needs a subject of two or more. 我 is only one person.

exercises.en: My friend and I are both students.
why: 和 joins the two nouns 我 and 我朋友, and 都 then says "both".
也 must come after the full subject and before the verb. It can't join 我 and 我朋友.
都 already appears before 是. It can't also join the two nouns; that is the job of 和.
都 means "all" and goes after the plural subject 我们, right before 是.
和 joins two nouns. Here there is only one subject, 我们, and a verb follows.
很 is used before adjectives like 好 or 大, not before 是.
Correct: 都 comes after the subject 我们 and before the verb 喜欢.
都 can't come after the verb. It must go before 喜欢.
都 never starts the sentence. Put it after the subject 我们.

exercises.prompt: Which means 'She is a teacher too'?
why: 也 can't start the sentence. It goes after the subject 她.
也 must come before the verb 是, not after it.
Correct: subject 她, then 也, then the verb 是.
和 means "and" between nouns. It doesn't mean "too" and can't come before a verb.

exercises.instruction: Add 都 to say that both of them are doctors.
why: Correct: 都 comes after the whole subject 爸爸和妈妈 and before the verb 是.
都 must come before the verb 是, not after it.
都 can't start the sentence. It sums up the people mentioned before it.
都 can't split 爸爸和妈妈. It goes after the whole subject.

exercises.instruction: Join the two sentences into one with 和.
exercises.source: 我喜欢苹果。我喜欢包子。
options: 我喜欢苹果和我喜欢包子。
why: Correct: 和 joins the two nouns 苹果 and 包子 after one verb.
和 can't join two whole sentences. Join just the nouns: 苹果和包子.
和 must stand between two nouns. Here it is placed before the verb 喜欢.

exercises.instruction: Make it negative so it means 'None of us drink tea.'
why: Correct: 不 goes right before the verb, after 都: 都不喝.
不 must come before the verb 喝, not after it.
不 can't start the sentence. Put it after 都 and before the verb.

exercises.en: Mom and Dad are both at home.
exercises.why: 和 joins the two nouns, and 都 comes after the whole subject, before the verb 在.
也 goes after the subject and before the verb 是.
